head: 0b0949a420c0cac8311b83fdc9b77c872c775056
scope: The whole branch against workspace, 5721e4aad..0b0949a42. An independent reviewer read the full diff of df114cfd1 and 3ddedb1f1: deliver.py's changed_bases, branch_lines, epic_bases, ready_merges and survey, probing one, zero and several bases, unplanned rows joined to engineering rows, missing --engineering and a legacy engineering base or pull request; it read the callers in sync.py (compose_id, the landed rule) and board.py, Deliver's Run Delivery Session, Task Merge, Epic Integration, Delivery Brief and Unit Dispatch, and grepped the whole skill for prose routing engineering through a base or pull request. 0b0949a42 fixes its eight findings; the session re-read that delta in full: only a unit changing engineering alone links a commit, so compose_id never meets a commit beside --link and a commit never delivers a row that also has a pull request.
criteria: AC1: test_a_unit_changing_only_engineering_pushes_it_with_no_branch shows an engineering-only row, in an epic of one base and of three, as 'push engineering' with no branch; Deliver step 7 and 10 deliver it by its push and Task Merge. AC2: test_an_engineering_epic_base_is_neither_required_nor_taken shows --bases with i07/e00/engineering ignored and no undeclared line; Prepare Delivery Bases, Epic Bases and Changed Branches exclude the branch. AC3: test_an_epic_changing_engineering_and_main_merges_into_main_alone offers a merge into i07/e00/main alone; an epic's review pull requests are one per base, and engineering has none. AC4: Planning Records states the rule; Publish Planning Record, Prepare Delivery Bases, Task Branches, Delivery Plan, Task Delivery, Task Merge and Deliver link it; the checker resolves every link; Commit Planning Record's restatement is gone.
validation: At 0b0949a42: planner suite 1180 tests OK (1 skipped); shared suite 295 tests OK; check_skill_files.py skills/work-planner 65 files, 0 findings; git diff --check clean; pull_request_body.py on the body: no findings.

findings.description: Sync Epic's compose_id exits on a row holding an engineering commit link when --link adds a pull request, so a unit changing engineering and main could not record delivery.
A pushed engineering commit linked beside an open pull request marked a mixed row delivered before its pull request merged.
An epic whose rows change engineering alone had no route past Epic Integration in Task Merge.
Deliver step 6 pushed engineering files before the unit's tests ran, and step 8 named no route for a fix to them.
Deliver steps 7 and 10 placed the no-pull-request exception mid-list rather than as a gate.
Delivery Brief Work Identity and Unit Dispatch assumed at least one task branch and unit checkout.
Epics of one or no base now read work items and need --engineering; the pull request body must state it.
Task Merge step 3 stated a fact rather than a step for a push.
